name: u00
explanation: Fires inside a rule, requirement, permission or prohibition in formal legal, licensing, regulatory, eligibility or offer-terms text. It peaks on the operative word: a deontic modal or its predicate (must, may be reproduced), a scoping quantifier (ANY), the 'or' of an eligibility threshold ('16 years or more/older'), or a compliance word ('complies with'), and stays moderately active through the rest of the rule clause, including its closing period. The same words in narrative, past-tense or epistemic use ('documents were submitted', 'she must be tired', 'started with') stay weak, under about a quarter of the maximum.

name: u01
explanation: Fires on a word-internal subword piece (a token with no leading space) that directly follows the opening fragment of a word the tokenizer splits into two or more pieces, e.g. 'el' in 'nov|el', 'on' in ' ax|on', 'rom' in ' K|rom|berg', 'ogen' in ' pharmac|ogen|etic'. It peaks on that first continuation piece, usually 1-4 letters, in rare names and technical or foreign words, and stays near zero on single-token whole words, on the word-start fragment itself, and mostly on closing suffix pieces such as 'ic', 'etic', 'berg' or 'ment'.

name: u02
explanation: Fires on mathematical extremum/limit operators -- sup, inf, lim, max, min, written as LaTeX (\sup, \max_{...}) or as words in math prose ('the inf of g') -- peaking on the operator token and staying high on its following subscript '_{', index variable and closing '}' or on the 'of' that introduces its argument. Other operators (\sum, \log, \alpha), non-math uses of 'max' (Max Planck, 'max speed'), and ordinary prose stay weak (below ~0.3 of max); math-question words such as 'factor', 'divisor', 'which of the' give only moderate activity.

name: u03
explanation: Fires on the second (completing) token of a noun-phrase collocation or proper name that opens a text, e.g. a title or headline start like 'Tony Abbott', 'Jake Jones', 'Further studies', 'short party', 'Weekly Vote', or a word-piece completing the first word ('Imm|une', 'J|abal'). Strength falls off within the first few tokens: the same name deep in a sentence is weak, and verbs, function words and non-collocating continuations at position 1 ('Tony said', 'I think', 'Of course') stay near zero. Every first token sits at a ~0.15 floor.

name: u04
explanation: Fires on the second piece of a tightly bound multi-token unit, i.e. a subword or word that completes a stem or fixed phrase begun by the previous token (jur|or, apolog|ises, Südamer|ika, Tari|q, Once| Upon, looking| for, heard| of, works| fine, general| counsel, Juan| Carlos); it stays near zero on the stem token itself and on free-standing content words, and is strongest for 'or' in 'juror' (~1.0 of max).

name: u05
explanation: Fires inside capitalized titles of works (songs, films, books) that are worded as a clause rather than a noun phrase. It peaks on the pronoun, verb or function word just after the title's first word (It [Comes], Did I Tell [You], If [This] is a Man, She [Loves] You, You [Are] Here, Here [With] You). Noun-phrase titles (The Long Road, Star Wars) and the same words in lowercase prose stay weak. A second, weaker trigger is the deictic word that ends spoken phrases such as "it's like this/that" and "built this way".

name: u06
explanation:
Fires on a single line-break token (a bare '
', or a punctuation+'
' token like ':
'/'.
' more weakly) that ends a short standalone line such as a section heading, label or number ('History', 'References', 'External links', '1927') and is immediately followed by content on the next line rather than a blank line; strongest when the bare '
' directly follows the heading word. It is near zero on double newlines ('

'), on ordinary prose sentences that wrap with a single newline, and on all non-newline tokens.

name: u07
explanation: Fires on the fragments of a random-looking alphanumeric code inside a URL path or query (t.co / bit.ly short links, YouTube v= IDs, jsbin IDs), strongest on the first few code tokens right after the '/' or '=' and fading toward the end of the code. It stays near zero on ordinary words in the same URL position (e.g. '/news', '/home') and is weaker on the same code outside a URL. Separately it fires strongly on the first token of a text (e.g. '#', 'package', 'def', 'The', 'I') and on little else in plain prose.

name: u08
explanation: Fires on the first sub-word token of a word the tokenizer splits into several pieces, when that token is a fragment that cannot stand as a complete word in context (e.g. ' des'|picable, ' dece'|iving, ' t'|attered, ' spo'|ilt, ' D'|istinguished, ' co' before 'founded'), so the model must still complete the word; it is near zero on the continuation pieces and on whole single-token words in the same slot, and weaker when the first piece is itself a common word (' is'|chaemic, ' st'|ammer).

name: u09
explanation: Fires on the first token of the second number in a range or list of event dates/days (the digit or space right after '-', ' to', ' through', ' and' in e.g. 'held June 12-14', 'September 3 through 6', '13 - 22'), most strongly when the context is a scheduled event (held/runs/takes place + month). Numeric ranges that are not dates (scores, percentages, page ranges like 135-161) give only weak activity (<0.4 of max), and the first number of the range and the separator itself are lower.

name: u10
explanation: Fires in Unix/sysadmin/scripting contexts (installing packages, configuring or scheduling software, shell output) on the token that names a system-level action or location the text is about to carry out: strongest on '/usr' opening a filesystem path after a shell command, and on the operative verb/particle of an install-or-schedule instruction ('setting up' a job for a script, 'restart' after installing into /usr/local/bin); the same words in non-technical prose ('setting up a tent', 'restart' after shelving a book) stay weak (<0.2 of max), and ordinary prose is near zero.

name: u11
explanation: Fires on the token that spells a word from the 'analy-' family (analysis, analyses, analyzed/analysed, analyze, analytical, analyst, Analytics), peaking on that word's own token and staying near zero on synonyms (evaluation, processed, collected) and on the following words; a weaker secondary trigger is a word-start or mid-word piece of a rare non-English proper name (' Bat' in Batembo, 'az' in Benazir, 'af' in Jaafar, ' Nim' in Nimr).

name: u12
explanation: Fires on the second token of a tight two-token unit, where the token completes something the previous token started: post-modifying degree 'enough' right after an adjective ('sharp enough', 'unusual enough', 'Funny enough'), a passive/past participle right after a be-verb or subject noun ('been made', 'was made', 'Data obtained'), '.com' right after 'github', and word-internal continuation pieces ('fire|proof', 'Har|sh', 'J|od'). It stays near zero on the same words when they don't complete such a unit: determiner 'enough' ('has enough money', 'not enough'), active 'made' ('She made'), '.com' after other domains (google, gitlab), and whole-word tokens.

name: u13
explanation: Fires on digit tokens of multi-digit coefficients inside long, generated-style algebra problems (e.g. 'Solve ... = -215*i - 4', 'Suppose ... - 4011 = -394*b'), peaking on the leading digit of a number on the right-hand side after '= -' once several multi-digit terms have already been read; strength grows with how much equation material precedes the digit. Digits in prose, in short isolated expressions, or with no preceding equation context stay weak (below ~0.3 of max), and non-digit tokens (variables, number words) in the same slot drop to the background level.

name: u14
explanation: Fires at the start of the category-name slot in a Wikipedia-style end-of-article category footer ('Category:<name>' lines, usually after References/External links): the ':' after 'Category' and the first one to three tokens of the name (in 'Category:19xx births/films/deaths' the peak is the '9', in 'Category:Living people' the ':'). It is weak (<0.2 of max) on the same years or words in prose, on non-'Category' labels like 'Tags:' (first line), and when the colon is missing; a weaker secondary response occurs on ' in' + space before a year in 'established/formed in 1948'.

name: u15
explanation: Fires on the token that sits inside a tightly constrained continuation that the context has set up: interior digits of an identifier or date the context has just introduced (a grant number after 'Advanced Grant', the year digits after 'born 28 July 19', a phone or patent number), and the linking function word of a fixed idiom ('nothing [to] do with', 'happy [to] receive', 'out [of] 10', 'Fill out [this] field'). It stays weak (<0.25 of max) on ordinary prose words and on the same digits or function words when no such frame comes before them (bare 'The year 1992', 'something to do', 'none to do').

name: u16
explanation: Fires on the token that completes an idiomatic degree/hedging noun-phrase frame: chiefly the ' a' in '(not/too) much of a', 'a bit of a', 'something of a', 'too fine a', and the ' deal' in '(no/a) big deal'. The same article or noun in a literal frame ('part of a', 'head of a', 'such a', 'made a deal', 'big win') stays near zero; the rest of the activity is weak token-identity firing on names/code identifiers (' Apache', ' IOException', ' Amazon').

name: u17
explanation: Dense feature that fires most strongly on the token that continues a stock boilerplate formula in web or technical text: the shell pipe ' |' after a command, the ')' closing a wire-service dateline '(Reuters)', a photo-credit ' Source' before ':', the ']' or '],' of [@B11]-style citation markers, the '0'/'1' of a 20xx year, ' Place' in the GNU licence address, '_now' in Django auto_now, a fixed compound such as arm+'bar'. The same slot filled with an ordinary, non-formulaic word gives only a weak to moderate activation (about 0.1-0.4 of max), and plain narrative prose stays near 0.

name: u18
explanation: Fires on the last piece of a word or fixed term that the tokenizer splits into fragments, at the token that completes it: 'V' in 'HBV', '-control' in 'form-control', 'ation' in 'alienation', 'ook' in 'undertook', 'ged' in 'double-edged', and also on the second word of a few fixed technical or official names ('United States', 'Visual Studio'). It is near zero on whole single-token words and on the opening fragment, and weak on ordinary two-word names like 'New York' or 'Supreme Court'.

name: u19
explanation: Fires on the head noun of a wh-determiner phrase ('what plant', 'which team', 'what new products', 'Which book') in an embedded or direct question: the noun right after interrogative 'what/which' (optionally past an adjective), peaking on that noun (~0.4-0.7 of max) with weak spill onto the next clause's subject/auxiliary; the same noun after 'the/that/a/if' stays near zero. Separately it has a diffuse, weaker response to some compound-name/identifier tokens (' Death' in 'Death Row', ' for' in 'Institute for', the space before ISBN/ID digits, code identifiers) that this rule does not cover.

name: u20
explanation: Fires on tokens inside a clause that admits a shortfall, failure or exception to an otherwise expected success: negated/limited ability or success ('don't always get it right', 'can't always handle', 'may not be', 'don't match up very well', 'got some things wrong', 'there's a problem with'), and frequency/exception hedges ('Sometimes,', 'some instances where'); it peaks on the word completing the shortfall (right/well/wrong/always/not/problem) and stays elevated on the next token or punctuation. The same affirmative clause without the negation, hedge or failure word is predicted near zero (it promotes failure/error tokens downstream); a secondary unrelated trigger is the last digit of a bracketed citation range like [@B6]-[@B8].

name: u21
explanation: Fires in scientific/technical prose (physics, chemistry, biomedicine) on the token that sits inside an unfinished technical noun phrase and sets up a specialised term: a connector after a technical word ('Solar[ and] Heliospheric', 'protons[ and]', 'from human' before leukocytes), an ion/element symbol after a technical modifier ('vacuolar[ H]+'), or the first subword of a rare jargon word ('[ ps]ammoma'). It is near zero in everyday prose, even on the same connector or symbol tokens ('Smith and', 'parents and', 'famous H').

name: u22
explanation: Fires on the token that opens the predicate or right-hand operand of a contrasting/opposing relation: the verb or auxiliary right after 'but <subject>' ("but that's/was", "but I've", "but the second returned", "but have"), the inequality operator '!=' (much more than '=='), and '+' inside an algebraic expression (more than '-' or '*'), i.e. the slot where a negating or contrasting continuation (not, no, nil, undefined, problems, zero) is expected. The same predicate token after 'and' or 'because' instead of 'but' fires roughly half as much or less, and content nouns, the subject itself and the continuation token after the peak stay near zero.

name: u23
explanation: Diffuse, broadly-on feature whose strong peaks come in formal reference phrases. It fires hardest on ' of'/' the' right after a numbered legal or document provision ('Article 9 of the', 'Section 22A of the', 'Title VII of the'), and on the token that completes a canonical official name or citation ('National Register of Historic Places', '477 F.2d'). Generic 'of the' with no numbered provision before it, and non-canonical completions ('Historic Homes'), stay at the low background (~0.2-0.4 of scale).

name: u24
explanation: Lookahead for the digit '1': the unit fires on the token just before a number (a space, ' (', '-' of a range, ' of') when the earlier text lets the model work out that the number will start with '1', e.g. a percentage or denominator implied by counts already given ('ignorance 4 (' -> 13.3% of 30; 'nine attacks, or approximately ' -> 16.6% of 54; 'CI = 2.35-' -> 15.88 given OR 6.1). It stays near zero before numbers whose predicted first digit is anything else, before non-numeric continuations, and in short contexts where the number is not inferable.

name: u25
explanation: Fires on an incomplete fragment inside a word the tokenizer splits into several pieces: usually the second piece (e.g. 'reme' in Sup|reme, 'arth' in Pr|arth|ana, 'ched' in Ens|ched|e, 'stay' in main|stay, 'command' in sub|command, 'rec' in antis|ec|rec|y), sometimes a rare word-initial stem like ' fiss', and also the attribute opener '="' after an HTML attribute name. Whole words that are a single token (Supreme, Amsterdam, Patricia, angry) and later suffix pieces ('ana', 'y', 'é') stay near zero.

name: u26
explanation: Fires on the word 'risk' in any sense (risk, risks, Risk, -risk, 'at risk', 'took a risk', 'market risk'), and peaks just as high or higher on the next token when it continues a risk compound: 'risk of', 'risk for', 'risk factor(s)', 'risk-group'. Close synonyms (danger, threat, chance) get a weaker version, mostly on the following 'of'; unrelated nouns and their 'of'/'factor' stay near zero.

name: u27
explanation: Fires on the last token of a clause's grammatical subject when that subject is a human agent or authority (a person's name, 'He'/'She' resuming a previously introduced official, or institutional nouns like officials/judge/court/board/minister), at the point just before the predicate verb, strongest in news or legal narrative about public figures; the same nouns as objects, or non-human subjects ('It', 'funds', 'weather'), stay weak.

name: u28
explanation: Fires inside visual-UI / presentation markup and styling code (Android layout XML, HTML head and Bootstrap grid classes, CSS color rules, hex color literals like 0xff0000) on the structural token that opens the next styling slot: the indentation/newline after a layout tag name or attribute line, the tag name 'meta', the ' #' after 'color:', the '-sm' in 'col-sm', the 'xff' of a 0xff color. It is near zero in prose and in markup/code without a visual-styling cue (e.g. 'margin:' or 'z-index' instead of 'color:', '<title' instead of '<meta', plain decimal numbers instead of 0xff hex, non-UI XML tags).

name: u29
explanation: Fires on the token right after a rare proper name or identifier that is split into several subword pieces (a tool, firm, package or variable name such as 'mencoder', 'KPMG', '$sessao'). That token is usually a connector or operator (' or', ' and', ',', ' =') or the first fragment of a quoted package or nickname (the 'j' of 'jekyll'). It stays near zero after common single-token words ('encoder', 'IBM', 'it') and in ordinary prose.

name: u30
explanation: Fires on a plural group-quantifier or plural pronoun that picks out a set of entities already introduced: a numeral or 'both' right after 'all'/'between the'/'within' ('in all three grades', 'between the three countries'), the contrastive 'some' in a 'some say..., others say..., some claim' enumeration, and the plural pronoun of a tag question ('..., do they?'). Singular or non-quantifier substitutes in the same slot ('do you', 'and claim', 'all the', 'each') are much weaker; ordinary content words are near zero.

name: u31
explanation: Polysemantic feature firing on a token from which a fixed, near-certain continuation follows. Its two strongest families: (1) ' it' right after 'when' in the idiom setup 'X when it [comes to]' (strong after a claim like 'is an expert / is neutral when it'; weak after 'if it', 'when he' or a plain temporal 'I like it when it rains'); (2) the leading digit '1' of a birth year inside a biographical parenthetical such as '(born July 8, 1938)' or '(3 May 1970 – ...)', but not a '2' leading digit or a bare year. Weaker hits: ' and' in 'born and raised', the boilerplate tokens of license headers. Generic idioms ('on the other hand', 'first and foremost') do not fire.

name: u32
explanation: A largely lexical feature that fires on a specific set of word-piece tokens, mostly an inner or second-to-last fragment of a rare multi-token proper noun or word ('oby' in Scooby, 'urch' in Murchison, 'le' in Hartlepool, 'al' in Rawalpindi, ' Olymp', ' earm', 'ym' in Ganymede, 'ar' in cerebellar, 'ber' in gibberish, 'mi' in Lakshmi) plus a few whole words (' turbo', ' Resident', ' odds', ' prime', ' hybrid', '.parallel', '.Virtual'). Peaks are about 0.5 to 0.9 of max; common words and other spellings in the same slot (Liverpool, Scrappy, helmets, fast) stay near 0. Only the preceding context changes the activation; text after the token has no effect. A sentence-initial 'The' before ' prime' or ' odds' weakens it, and a descriptive word before it ('artistic prime', 'also odds') strengthens it.

name: u33
explanation: Fires at the start of the second number in a numeric pair or range (e.g. '143-167', '18 and 65', '15 to 99'): moderately on the separator or space before it, and most strongly (often >0.6 of max) on the second number's first digit when that digit repeats the leading digit of the first number (the '1' in '143-1|67', the '5' in '543-5|67'); a different leading digit gives near zero on that digit. Outside numbers it fires weakly to moderately on predictable continuations in formulaic boilerplate (license text 'is located', 'is distributed').

name: u34
explanation: Fires on the token carrying the word stem 'pass' used as the word pass itself (verb forms ' pass', ' passed', ' passes', ' passing', also noun 'pass' in sports/code contexts, the name 'Pass(more)', and Portuguese/Spanish 'pass-/pasar'), strongest for inflected verb forms like 'passed'/'passes away'/'has passed'; it stays near zero on synonyms (crossed, died, went, skipping) and is weak (<0.15 of max) on derived words 'passage'/'passion' and on 'pass' as the head of a compound noun like 'boarding pass'.

name: u35
explanation: A dense feature (weak background on ~half of tokens) that fires most strongly on words describing how far back in time something has persisted or how open-ended a time span is: 'dates/goes back' and the following 'to/centuries' after a tradition/custom/practice subject, 'centuries (ago/old)', 'ago', and 'at any time'. The same verbs with a non-historical subject (an invoice, a road walking 'back home') or with a non-temporal complement ('in France', 'very old', 'at this time') stay near background (<0.3 of scale).

name: u36
explanation: Fires in geometry/layout specifications (UIKit frames, CGRectMake, rect(...), Android layout_*, CSS) on the token that opens the width/horizontal-size slot: the separator and space right after the x,y origin pair, before the third (width) number, the key 'width'/'_width', and 'wrap_content'; it fires more weakly on 'right' when it completes a 'left and right' pair in UI or arrow-key text. It stays near zero on the same numbers or words outside a geometry context (generic function arguments, 'turn right', 'wide' in prose).

name: u37
explanation: Fires on a non-final piece of a multi-token lexical unit whose continuation is tightly determined: the leading subword fragment of a word split into several tokens (reg|ener|able, spec|if|ity, discrim|inated, air|brushing, super|absorbent) or the modifier noun opening a fixed compound (water polo, Air Medals, electron microscope, aws|logs), peaking on that token and dropping on the completing piece. Whole single-token words and ordinary adjective+noun phrases stay near the baseline (~0.1 of scale), and degree words like 'too' fire only moderately.

name: u38
explanation: Fires on the token that completes a highly predictable, formulaic collocation set up by the preceding words: the strongly expected filler of a stock phrase ("tell/share with your [friends]", "pip [install]", "both ... [and]", "seeing that [guy]", "the document [states]", the next digit of a zip code or URL scheme). Activity scales with how expected the token is given its context; the same word in an unformulaic context, or an unexpected word in the slot, gives weak activation, and the setup words themselves stay low.

name: u39
explanation: Fires on a non-initial subword piece inside a word the tokenizer splits into several pieces (e.g. 'ARGET' in TARGETS, 'acter' in Agrobacterium, 'ial' in Dorsomedial, 'urally' in culturally, 'l' in Podlaski, 'a' in Whoa), and on the period of a title abbreviation like 'Mr.'. It is weak or silent on whole-word tokens and word-initial pieces, so the same word written as a single token, or replaced by a one-token word, does not activate it; secondary weaker activity on verb-particle heads like ' turn' in 'turn out'.

name: u40
explanation: Fires on the first token of a multi-word fixed technical term or proper name, at the point where a specific continuation is strongly expected (SQL 'SHOW' before SLAVE STATUS/TABLES, 'UN security' before council, 'VMware' before tools, 'File' before Descriptors, 'West' before Chester, word-initial pieces like ' gluc', ' pr'(sync), ' tr'(uetype)). It reacts to the token just read and is weak on the continuation and on ordinary lowercase prose words; uppercase SQL keyword 'SHOW' is the strongest trigger.

name: u41
explanation: Fires on the tokens of the second or later item in a parallel, list-like construction that repeats a template already seen earlier in the context, strongest on the leading digit of a repeated count/percentage statistic such as the '2' of '6 (20.0%)' after '21 (70.0%)', or the '-old' of '39-year-old' after '44-year-old'. The first instance of the template and text with no parallel structure are weak. A weaker, separate component fires on the second word of a fixed compound or name (code smell, Stack Overflow, victory lap, ORM Lite).

name: u42
explanation: Fires on a word-initial token that opens a multi-token unit whose completion is still pending and predictable: the first piece of a multi-token name or split word (' San'/' Santa' before a place name, ' su'+'isse', ' ped'+'idos', ' thé'+'olog', ' year'+'-upon-year') and, more weakly, a past auxiliary ' was'/' were' right after a pronoun subject ('I was hoping/trying'). It is near zero on completed single-token words (' Paris', ' Monaco', ' Los'-less names) and on the continuation pieces themselves ('isse', ' Francisco', ' Marino').

name: u43
explanation: Fires on the first token of the second element of a memorized fixed multi-token name or technical term (brand, title, Latin/anatomical phrase, hyphenated legal/role compound), at the point where the first element has been read and the token is an unfinished fragment whose completion is now determined (e.g. Coldwell ' Bank'(er), incertae ' sed'(is), Deathly ' Hall'(ows), sarcoplasmic ' ret'(iculum), Daler'-R'(owney), Plaintiff'-'(Appellee)). The same token in ordinary compositional text (a 'bank', town 'Hall', 'Daler and Rowney') is inactive, as are names whose second part is one complete token (Wells Fargo).

name: u44
explanation: Fires on the first token of a well-known multi-token name or fixed phrase, where that token alone points to one specific entity or completion (Bernie->Sanders, Mayor Pete->Buttigieg, Golden->Gate, Carnegie->Hall, cubic->inch, the '8' of an 18xx year). The peak is on that first token itself, not on the completion. Generic or common first names (John, Peter), plain adjectives (yellow) and the tokens that complete the name stay near zero. Activation is weak in very short contexts and grows with context.

name: u45
explanation: Fires on the digit tokens inside a written sum of money that is being paid, charged, fined, awarded or donated (after '$' or a pay/fine/sentence verb), peaking on the first digits right after '$' in legal-penalty amounts ('fined $7|5|0', 'a $7[[5]]0 fine') and on the inner zeros of comma-grouped thousands ('$44,0[[0]]0', '$50,0[[0]]0'). The same digits are weak or silent in non-monetary numbers: years ('2000', '1945'), page/room numbers, counts of objects ('30 seats'), and bare numbers without a money cue.

name: u46
explanation: Fires most strongly (about 0.5-0.9 of max) on the conjunction ' or' directly after a gendered personal pronoun in the gender-neutral doublet 'his or her' / 'he or she' / 'she or he' / 'him or her', mid-sentence. It stays weak (<0.2) on ' and', ' then' or other words in that slot, and on ' or' after non-pronouns ('tea or coffee', 'this or that', 'red or blue'). Activity elsewhere is diffuse and weaker (~0.2-0.5), for example ' to' in number ranges ('15 to 99') or ' (' before a percentage.

name: u47
explanation: Fires on a token that is an orphaned fragment at the start or inside an unpredictable, non-dictionary string: a bare space+capital-letter piece (' M', ' C', ' W') that begins a rare surname or acronym split into subwords (Rebecca M|ikesell, Jim C|ullom, of C|PO), and the digits/letters inside random hex, UUID, hash or ID codes (and the first digits after a phone-number area code). Common whole-word names (' Miller', ' Brown'), whole acronyms (' CEO'), ordinary prose and regular/repetitive numbers (years, 0000, 0.0250000) stay near zero.

name: u48
explanation: Dense, weak feature that peaks on the first digit of a numeric field that follows an earlier number inside a structured reference or boilerplate header: e.g. the volume number right after 'Year;' in a journal citation ('Med. 2019;[8]1:2551'), the year after 'Copyright' in license headers, and digits inside IDs/URLs; also on package-path segments after 'import' in code (' io', '.git'). The same digits in plain prose (prices, counts) or with the preceding year replaced by a word stay low (< ~0.35 of max).

name: u49
explanation: Fires on a token that is an incomplete word fragment, i.e. the first or a middle subword piece of a word the tokenizer splits (e.g. ' re' in 'resected', ' j' in 'jollity'/'josh', 'é' in 'Béla', 'oc' in 'thrombocytopenia', 'ella' in 'Trigonella', ' t' in Portuguese 'tive'), strongest in rare, technical, foreign or lowercase-name words; it also fires on French negation/auxiliary pieces ('ait', ' pas'). Whole common English words that are single tokens, and the final piece of a split word, stay low (below ~0.25 of max).

name: u50
explanation: Fires on the modifier word (adjective, quantifier or noun premodifier such as 'full', 'great', 'real', 'similar', 'any', 'accordance') that immediately follows the preposition 'in' (optionally 'in a/an/his'), when 'in' follows a verb or clause and opens an adverbial manner/degree idiom ('in full force', 'in great detail', 'in real time', 'in a similar way', 'in accordance with'); it is near zero when the same modifier follows another preposition ('with', 'at') or no preposition, and weak for locative 'in a big house' or a bare noun right after 'in' ('in detail', 'in Paris').

name: u51
explanation: Fires on the first token of a lexicalized multi-token unit whose continuation is highly predictable: word-initial subword fragments of a longer word (' inf'|'arction', ' spring'|'ing', ' plug'|'-ins', '_BACK'|'WARD', 'PS'|'DB'), the head verb of a fixed passive/phrasal construction ('was followed' up/by), and an opening ' (' right after a technical term that introduces its abbreviation ('Hepatitis B virus (' HBV). Plain content words in ordinary prose, and ' (' after a verb, stay low (<0.3 of max).

name: u52
explanation: Fires at the token ' best' (English superlative 'best' and the Germanic subword ' best' in Danish 'bestod' / German 'bestehen') and at inflections of the verb 'go' (' go', ' goes', ' going', ' went', ' gone'), especially 'went/gone/goes through/against' and 'go to'; synonyms that replace these words ('well', 'new', 'great', 'been', 'came', 'runs', 'walk', 'kom') are predicted weak (under ~0.35 of max), and other text stays mostly low with only diffuse sub-0.6 background activity.

name: u53
explanation: Fires on the first tokens of the predicate (the finite verb, auxiliary/modal, negation or degree adverb right after the subject) in an expository, generic or modal claim about how an inanimate thing, substance, technique or code object behaves (e.g. 'fertilizers [do] not', 'string refs [have] some issues', 'the f/stop could [greatly] increase'). It is weak or absent when the subject is a person, when the clause is an episodic past-tense event, inside 'that'-relative clauses, and on the subject noun itself.

name: u54
explanation: Fires on the second noun of a two-sided evaluative pair of the form 'a/the [positive] and/but/or a [negative]' (e.g. 'a blessing and a curse', 'a gift and a curse', 'a strength and a weakness', 'a success and a failure'), firing strongly only when that noun completes the contrast; the same noun on its own ('It is a curse') or after a neutral first item ('a pen and a pencil', 'a blessing and a coat') stays near zero, and ordinary antonym coordinations of adjectives ('good and evil', 'rich and poor') stay low. A weaker second facet fires on the inner digits of numbers in citation and page-range contexts (the second number of 'pp 135-161', years after a page range).

name: u55
explanation:
Fires on the line-break or sentence-final punctuation token at the end of a line that announces embedded non-prose content, most strongly in technical, help-forum or patent text when that line names an image, screenshot or figure (e.g. 'Here is the image
', 'Here is a screenshot
', '...shown in FIG. 1.'), i.e. where a markdown image or link bracket '[' / '![](' would come next. It is weak on line breaks after other announcements ('Here is my question
', 'Here is the error
') and near zero on sentence ends in casual narrative prose or mid-line positions.

name: u56
explanation: Fires on the predicate word of a statement that assigns accountability, obligation, primacy or validity to a subject, i.e. the head after a copula/'have'/adverb in frames like 'X is responsible for', 'X has a responsibility to', 'first and foremost', 'the same is true of', 'is serious', 'must always', 'X's first priority'; the same words used attributively or outside such an assertive predicate frame ('the responsible party', 'the true story', 'true that') are weak, and near-synonyms without the accountability/primacy sense ('grateful', 'desire', 'last', 'said') are inactive. Secondary weaker trigger: the leading digit of CSS/class numeric values (width: 100%, col-sm-3).

name: u57
explanation: Fires on a determiner/particle that opens the object right after a verb, strongest by far on the French indefinite/partitive article 'des' (or elided 'd'' after 'pas') introducing a verb's object ('ont des', 'mangent des', 'il y a des': ~0.6-1.0 of max), and weakly (~0.1-0.3) on English 'in' and especially the following 'the' when 'in' is a verb particle/complement directly after a verb ('cram in', 'rake in the', 'called in the', 'join in the'). It is near zero on 'des' as the contraction de+les after a noun ('prix des'), on 'the' directly after a verb with no 'in' ('read the', 'join the'), and after other particles ('out the', 'up the').

name: u58
explanation: Fires on the second (completing) token of a tightly bound multi-token expression or idiom whose first part was just read, i.e. a token that the preceding word(s) make highly predictable: 'missing/miss [out]', 'on their [own]', 'operating [system]', 'Department of [Health]', 'proverb[ial]', 'Object[/]Relational', '(End' of Life, 'length +[ ]1', '= [-]1'. The same token after a word that does not bind it into a fixed phrase ('carrying out', 'his bike', 'favorite system') is weak, and function words ('of', 'the', 'or', 'a') are near zero.

name: u59
explanation:
Fires on a bare single-newline token '
' that directly follows a word or number (not merged with punctuation like '.
', '?
', '):
'), i.e. a line break that cuts the text without sentence-final punctuation, most strongly when it splits a clause mid-sentence (e.g. 'have to
change', 'take the
number') or ends an unpunctuated line such as a verse line or a math answer ('True
', '-18
'). Punctuation-merged newline tokens, '

', and all ordinary word tokens stay near zero.
